final_answer:
Condition C2 was compared with vector RAG (SS) on comprehensiveness for both the Podcast and News datasets. For the Podcast dataset, all global search conditions, including C2, had greater comprehensiveness than SS, with statistically significant differences (p < .05) in all cases [2]. Similarly, for the News dataset, all global search conditions, including C2, had greater comprehensiveness than SS, with statistically significant differences (p < .05) in all cases [2]. 

The average number of extracted claims, representing the claim-based measure of comprehensiveness, was higher for C2 than for SS in both datasets, with C2 showing 31.62 extracted claims for News and 32.46 for Podcast, compared to SS's 25.23 for News and 26.50 for Podcast [2]. These results align with the LLM-based win rates from Experiment 1, where global approaches achieved comprehensiveness win rates between 72-83% for Podcast transcripts and 72-80% for News articles [1].

However, there were no statistically significant differences observed among the global search conditions or between global search and source text summarization (TS) for comprehensiveness [4]. 

In conclusion, condition C2 outperformed vector RAG (SS) in comprehensiveness for both the Podcast and News datasets, but there were no significant differences between C2 and other global search conditions.
